relevance_note: Case series of three Chinese patients with PAPA syndrome and PSTPIP1 variants plus a literature table of 36 published cases: "The PSTPIP1 A230T mutation was identified in two patients, and a novel Y119C variation was revealed in a sporadic patient."
method_note: Read the paper in full; a Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON, and its transcription of Table 2 (36 literature cases: author, case no., variants, clinical characteristics, responses) was checked against the table row by row. Scope: Patients 1-3 (first-hand), plus mother and uncle of Patient 2 (affected relatives in the PSTPIP1 A230T family), plus the 36 literature cases of Table 2 (labelled 'Table 2 #<case no.>', all listed as PAPA patients; cases 15, 16, 28, 31 and 32 have no printed variant and get no variant rows). Merge decision: Patient 2's pedigree text mentions 'one of her cousins also complained of recurrent arthritis accompanied by fever'; I treated this as Patient 3 (the cousin of patient 2 with arthritis and fever) and created no separate row; the 'four affected kindreds' carrying c.688G>A were read as Patient 2, her mother, her uncle and this cousin/Patient 3, so heterozygous zygosity for mother, uncle and Patient 3 rests on that named group statement. Patient 2 inheritance left 'not reported': the paper never states by name that the mother carries the variant (only via the four affected kindreds). Patient 1's parents (deceased, untested, no autoinflammatory history) and healthy members of Patient 2's family get no rows. Group-level literature mentions (Laberko's five PAMI patients, adult-onset counts, Table 1 'Literature (n = 63)' column) get no rows. Table 2 rows with an empty Author cell (cases 9-12, 20-23, 26-27, 31-32) were given the author of the row above (visual grouping) in source_reference_in_review, quoting both rows; Table 2 lacks a gene column, so gene_symbol PSTPIP1 is supported by Table 1's 'PSTPIP1 variations' row, and for case 1's intronic variants by the reference title of ref (2). Variants 'A230 T' (cases 25-27) kept as printed with the space. Table 1 uses '–' in the triad-completeness rows without a legend; treated as not reported. Table 1 'No' cells (acne, PG, fever, other skin lesions) treated as explicit absence. Normal panels (CBC, biochemistry panel, urine analysis) were recorded as 'abnormal ...' excluded per D-27 but not used to exclude anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia or kidney involvement. Contradiction: Patient 2 has 'Hypochromic microcytic anemia (Hb 86g/L)' yet 'The CBC ... were normal'; both rows emitted and the anemia checklist item set to not reported. Patient 1: text describes 'blister-like rashes' while Table 1 lists 'Pustular rash'; both recorded. Age at last evaluation is the age at presentation (49/34/26 years); a 1-year follow-up is mentioned for Patient 1 without age. Literature checklist: Case 7 'resembling IBD' not counted as IBD (hedged); 'recurrent otitis'/'OM' not counted as recurrent infections; case 2 'pyogenic osteomyelitis' counted under sterile osteomyelitis item. Age at onset for Patient 2 comes from Table 1 (24 years) since the text gives none. The abstract says 76 literature patients in 29 articles; cohort_size_as_stated is the 3 patients of this centre.

span: This is, by far, the largest case series of PAPA syndrome from China to the best of our knowledge.
Herein we reported three adult patients with PAPA syndrome from two unrelated families in China and conducted a review of the literature.
A total of three patients were diagnosed with PAPA syndrome at our center from 2018 to 2020.
The PSTPIP1 A230T mutation was identified in two patients, and a novel Y119C variation was revealed in a sporadic patient.
